messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Patient Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Patient Name]
Admission Date: [Admission Date]
Discharge Date: [Discharge Date]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to the hospital due to lower extremity swelling and pain for four days. Physical examination revealed left lower limb pitting edema and calf tenderness. Color Doppler ultrasound showed an extensive DVT affecting the common iliac, external iliac and common femoral vein as well as superficial femoral down to popliteal vein. Treatment included bed rest, elevation with bandaging of left leg, and low molecular weight heparin injections. Investigations revealed no underlying etiology. Abdominal and pelvic US and CT scan showed an impacting stone and a severe left hydroureteronephrosis with almost lost of cortical thickness. Percutaneous nephrostomy was performed to decompress the hydronephrotic kidney. JJ stent was inserted and subsequently removed. Six weeks later, Doppler US showed complete recanalization of the superficial femoral, popliteal as well as the proximal segment of deep veins of the leg but common iliac, external iliac and common femoral veins and proximal superficial femoral vein were still partially thrombosed. Through pneumatic lithotripsy, the stone was fragmented under spinal anesthesia. Three months after that, Doppler US showed complete recanalization of iliac vessels.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
Treatment included bed rest, elevation with bandaging of left leg, and low molecular weight heparin injections. Percutaneous nephrostomy was performed to decompress the hydronephrotic kidney. JJ stent was inserted and subsequently removed. Pneumatic lithotripsy was performed to fragment the stone under spinal anesthesia. The patient was discharged on oral anticoagulation in the form of rivaroxaban 20 mg daily.

Follow-up:
The patient is advised to have regular follow-up visits with their healthcare provider.

Signed by: [Healthcare Provider Name and Title]

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
I80 is the best fit for the principal diagnosis: the admission was for the extensive left lower limb deep vein thrombosis (iliofemoral), which falls under phlebitis and thrombophlebitis. The obstructing ureteric stone with hydronephrosis (N13 / N20) was found during the workup as the likely underlying cause, but the presenting problem and the main treatment focus (anticoagulation, with the thrombosis monitored over follow-up) was the DVT. Deep vein thrombosis of the lower limb is coded I80 in ICD-10 and I80 in ICD-10-AM, which also covers the femoral and iliac veins. In ICD-10-AM the codes for DVT are I80.1 (femoral vein) and I80.2 (other deep vessels of lower extremities). So the category is I80.

**I80**
